name: Sway
summary: A wlroots-based Wayland compositor and i3-compatible tiling window manager that combines protocol surfaces, a hierarchical container tree, seat input, output management, IPC, and explicit lifecycle handling.

features.name: wlroots-backed Wayland compositor
features.description: Sway builds a Wayland compositor around wlroots, handling client protocols, surfaces, outputs, input seats, and backend events while applying Sway's policy and configuration.
benefits: Reuses common Wayland backend and protocol implementations
Keeps compositor policy and client resource ownership explicit
costs: Sway behavior depends on wlroots lifecycle and backend contracts
A compositor failure can terminate the managed session

features.name: Hierarchical container tree
features.description: Sway represents views, containers, workspaces, and outputs in a hierarchical tree with split orientations, tabbed or stacked arrangements, floating containers, focus, and geometry managed by tree operations.
benefits: Makes placement and focus composable through nested containers
Preserves i3-compatible layout and command concepts on Wayland
costs: Tree mutation must maintain parent, focus, geometry, and workspace invariants
Nested layouts make failure and configuration diagnosis more involved

features.name: Seat input and binding routing
features.description: Sway models keyboards, pointers, touch devices, and seats, applies input configuration and bindings, and routes events or commands to the focused container, workspace, or output.
benefits: Unifies device configuration, focus, and command dispatch
Allows input actions to manipulate the same tree used for rendering and IPC
costs: Device hotplug and seat focus add asynchronous state transitions
Binding precedence and input configuration can make actions difficult to debug

features.name: Output and render-resource management
features.description: Sway manages outputs, workspaces, views, surfaces, frame scheduling, and wlroots render resources; output geometry and visibility are derived from the container tree and output configuration.
benefits: Provides per-output workspace and geometry policy
Lets the compositor coordinate frame presentation with surface damage and layout changes
costs: Output hotplug, scaling, and render failures require coordinated tree and focus updates
Backend resource constraints can limit otherwise valid layouts

features.name: IPC command and lifecycle failure boundary
features.description: Sway exposes a command and event IPC protocol over compositor state and handles view, output, input, and backend lifecycle events; an individual client or output can disappear while the tree and compositor remain active, subject to backend failure handling.
benefits: Makes automation and status observation explicit at a stable command boundary
Separates many resource disconnects from global compositor lifecycle
costs: IPC clients must handle event ordering and command errors
Not every backend or protocol failure is isolated from the compositor process

mathematical_views.question: Which focus, split, workspace, floating, and output arrangements are reachable after tree commands and view lifecycle events?
assumptions: Containers are nodes with parent and child relations
Commands and lifecycle events are state transitions
Renderer details are abstracted from geometry derivation

mathematical_views.question: How do clients, views, surfaces, seats, outputs, and wlroots backend resources connect during input and frame presentation?
assumptions: Seats and outputs are typed compositor resources
Protocol and backend callbacks are graph edges

mathematical_views.question: How do view, output, input, IPC, and backend events move Sway between configured, active, disconnected, and failed states?
assumptions: Resource lifecycles are distinct from the process lifecycle
IPC errors are modeled as command-level outcomes
This view does not prove recovery from backend-wide faults

benefits: Common backend primitives reduce compositor implementation duplication
costs: Sway inherits backend and protocol coupling through wlroots

benefits: Nested tiling and familiar i3-compatible operations are explicit
costs: Tree invariants and nested focus behavior increase mutation complexity

benefits: Input policy and layout commands share one focus model
costs: Hotplug and binding precedence create asynchronous edge cases

benefits: Output geometry and frame resources are coordinated with layout
costs: Output and render failures complicate state consistency

benefits: Automation observes and controls compositor state through a protocol
costs: Event ordering and command errors become client responsibilities
